title: Keeping HELM simple
summary: HELM 1.0.1 is easier to read and use, with simpler principles, practical guides, shared skills, and a focused roadmap.

items.text: Start with six principles written in everyday language, each with a small action to try. The guides explain how to use the advice with your team.
The guides are easier to navigate, read on smaller screens, use with a keyboard, and share in a team discussion.
Further reading offers extra context and simple reminders for adapting the guidance without presenting every suggestion as a guaranteed result.
Choose a skill and your role to get practical steps, an example, an exercise for your next task, and a short self-check.

links.label: Find a guide for your skill and role

items.text: The roadmap focuses on making the current guidance clearer, trying a short shared-skills discussion, and considering a small playbook for one piece of work.
Follow one dated update with direct links to everything included in this release, or subscribe to future published updates.

title: A shared starting point for human–agent teamwork
summary: The first numbered release brings HELM’s principles, practical guides, and role descriptions together, so your team can refer to the same version when discussing how to work with AI agents.

sections.heading: A common language for your team

items.text: Explore six principles for decisions about AI-assisted work, from choosing simple approaches to keeping people accountable for results.
Use the Practitioner Guide to discuss how agents fit a workflow, how results should be checked, and where people need to make decisions.
Explore ownership, adoption, and measurement with the Leadership Guide, including questions to consider as your team changes how it works.
Explore how responsibilities and competencies may change across engineering, product, and design when agents become part of the work.
This release established a common reference for discussion and local testing. Teams still needed to try the guidance against their own work, and several recommendations were scheduled for review.
